web_events.answer: The U.S. economy expanded at a sluggish 1.5% pace in the second quarter, according to the latest GDP report. Consumer spending remained strong, increasing at a healthy 3.4% annual rate. The GDP growth decelerated from the 2.1% pace in the first quarter. Treasury yields remained steady as investors awaited more economic data releases, including the second quarter GDP estimate and July's personal consumption expenditure reading, which is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge.

web_events.query: China PMI economic data this week
web_events.answer: China's industrial profit growth in July slowed to 11.2% from a year earlier, marking a 7-month low and down from the 15.1% increase in June. For the first seven months of the year, profits climbed 17.6% from the previous year, showing a slowdown from the 18.7% growth in the first half. This deceleration is attributed to weakening domestic demand and external uncertainties including trade tensions and geopolitical risks.
